steps.text: Combine flour and salt in a medium bowl. Add shortening and mix with a fork or pastry blender until the mixture is very crumbly. Sprinkle ice-cold water over the mixture, 1 tablespoon at a time, stirring lightly with a fork after each addition, just until a small amount of dough holds together when gently squeezed. You may not need the full 1/2 cup.
Roll dough gently on a floured pastry cloth to about 1 inch larger than your pie plate.

Fold dough carefully in half and transfer to the pie plate; unfold and gently press into the bottom and sides. For a single-crust pie, trim dough to about 1/2 inch beyond the rim, fold the overhang under, and flute or crimp as desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Pie Crust
raw_recipe.description: The best pie crust recipe makes a flaky, tender crust every time with a perfect ratio of flour, shortening, and water—easy to roll, freeze, and bake.

review.reviewBody: fantastic pie crust! not too greasy, very easy to work with and very, very flaky. one quick note from past experiences, add the ice water one tablespoon at a time and toss with a fork after each addition.

Very good! I added a couple tsp. of white sugar to give it a little extra sweetness. They say the sugar makes the dough stickier and harder to work with and to add confectioners sugar instead, but it seemed to work out fine for me. I used tips from this site and froze the shortening (use butter flavored...great taste!) before cutting it into the flour (it doesn't freeze, it just gets very cold) and I used ICE water. I then refrigerated for 30 minutes prior to rolling out. After I rolled it and placed it in the pan, I refrigerated another 30 minutes before putting my filling in (pumpkin..YUM!). This resulted in a good tasting, flaky crust.

I hate making pie crust cause they never turn out. After watching on how to make a pie crust video on this site, I sucked it up and went for it. I decided to make a recipe & a 1/2 so I can have some for the top. I used unsalted butter instead of shortening. Mixed the cold cut butter with the flour & salt. Slowly added the ice water with a teaspoon till the dough stuck together by hand. Used about 5-6 teaspoons of water. Divided the dough and wrapped them in plastic and refridgerated them for about 1 hour. Took them out and rolled the bottom pie crust on a silpath so I didn't need to add extra flour. Placed the crust in the pie pan and molded it. Rolled the second dough and used cookie cutters for the top decorations. Refridgerated both crust for 30 minutes then added my fresh blackberry filling. After it was done and cooled, my husband, who loves pie crust more than the pie, gave me a big thumbs up. This will be my staple crust, when I have time to make it. Thanks!

All my life I have only made one pastry recipe: My Dad's. But now I live in China and don't have convenient access to shortening or lard and made this recipe with butter.

 I actually used a hand mixer to knead it, and it actually made the gluten come out (read: stretchy) and it was the easiest pastry I have ever worked with, even when melding the scraps together for a second round of rolling. Super happy with the result, my butter tarts popped out of the non-stick pan with such ease and no breakage. Super flaky, perfection. I will only use this recipe from now on.

Wonderful flakey crust that you can't mess up if you tried. I've made it as written, used Butter, used up to 1/4 c sugar when filling with bittersweet mousse, and have rolled it as well as pressed it into muffin tins to make mini fruit pies. When baking before adding filling, I bake at 400 degrees for 10+ minutes after pricking fork holes in the bottom. You can't go wrong with this!

This worked out gorgeously. It didn't take me that long to whip up, it tasted awesome and the recipe was very versatile. I can't really see how you can go wrong with this- If it's crumble-ey, add more water. If you add a little too much and it's too moist, rub it with some flour and use it for the top crust. I recommend making two separate batches- first batch for the bottom crust and the second batch for the top crust. 
This is my go-to recipe for crusts! Don't ask me why you'd wanna (impulse, maybe?), but this crust also works/tastes well with flavorings added. I added butter flavoring and it was pretty good!
I substitute butter for shortening and add 3 T of sugar and 1 tsp of vanilla. Cook time varies from 10-15 minutes depending on thickness at 350

I have always been intimidated by making my own pie crust. Saw this recipe and got courageous enough to try it. Imade this with Crisco shortening. Popped it in the fridge for about 30 minutes. Rolled it between pieces of wax paper . Used a cup to make mini pie crusts and put them in large cupcake tins. Added my filling and cut pie crust cut into strips, placed on top in a lattice pattern. Turned out very nice. Thanks for the recipe! I will use it again. And I am no longer scared to make my own pie crusts. Woot woot!

I love this pie crust! All I did was throw everything into my food processor, whiz it up until it came together, and BAM! instant pie crust. I also used butter flavoured Becel instead of shortening, just my personal preference.

I usually don't have much luck with pie crusts, but I needed two for Thanksgiving, so I gave this recipe my best shot. I made a double recipe, and before starting I had the shortening in the freezer all day. Without a pastry cutter or food processor, I cut up the shortening in the flour using a pizza cutter. I put ice water in by the tablespoon, adding about 2/3 cup in total, and tossing the mixture with a fork after each addition. I put the dough in the freezer for about 30 minutes before I rolled it out.
absolutely fantastic and easy. I let the dough chill forn30 minutes and used butter flavored Crisco. super flaky crust
I make apple pie and I use this pie crust recipe all the time very plain and simple love it
The crust was buttery and flaky. I used it for a peach cobbler
Great recipe
Good clear instructions. Comes together very easily. As noted all the water is not required. Lovely crust. Here is my blackberry pie.
Does not really work. Had to add extra water to roll....after baking it pulls away from top/edge making it smaller. Followed recipe to a tee. Will go back to my old recipe.
